summary: In San Jose, a Level 1 (120-volt) charger plugged into an existing outlet needs no permit; a Level 2 (240-volt) charger or any new outlet needs an electrical permit.

outcomes.explanation: A Level 1 charger that plugs into a standard 120-volt outlet you already have needs no permit. Installing a new outlet for it needs an electrical permit.
A Level 2 (240-volt) charger needs an electrical permit. If the manufacturer specifies mechanical ventilation, a mechanical permit is also required.

default_explanation: Installing a new outlet or circuit for a charger needs an electrical permit in San Jose. State law requires the city to approve charging-station applications through a building permit or similar nondiscretionary permit.
permit_types: Mechanical permit (if the manufacturer specifies mechanical ventilation)
fee_note: San Jose's FY 2025-26 fee schedule bills electrical inspection at a minimum of $315 per hour, with a 30-minute default minimum per item, in addition to the permit issuance fee.
docs_required: UL 2202 listing number (or another approved testing laboratory's listing) for the charging equipment, provided to the inspector
Panel rating, charging load, and circuit size
Whether a second electric meter will be installed
Location of the utility panel and the charger (EVSE)

notes.text: For a Level 2 installation, provide the inspector with the UL 2202 listing, the panel rating, charging load and circuit size, whether a second meter will be installed, and the panel and charger locations.
Single-family homes and duplexes can get the EV charger permit online at SJPermits.org.
DC fast chargers (Level 3) are not allowed on residential properties.
State law limits the city's review of a charging station application to health and safety requirements.
State law required cities with 200,000 or more residents to adopt an expedited, checklist-based permit process for EV charging stations by September 30, 2016.

For 1 to 25 chargers at one site, state law deems an application complete 5 business days after submission, and approved 20 business days after it is deemed complete, when the statute's other conditions are met.
The city cannot make permit approval depend on approval by a homeowners association.
Fees: electrical inspection is a minimum of $315 per hour with a 30-minute default minimum per item, plus a permit issuance fee.

Online permits can be pulled only by the property owner or a qualified contractor. The city recommends that a licensed contractor pull the permit; an owner-builder must also submit the Owner Acknowledgement and Information Verification Form, show ID at issuance, and be the owner of record.
San Jose adopted the 2025 California Electrical Code; the 2025 codes apply to permit applications made on or after January 1, 2026.

citations.code_section: Cal. Gov. Code §65850.7(g)(1)(A)
citations.quote: On or before September 30, 2016, every city, county, or city and county with a population of 200,000 or more residents, and, on or before September 30, 2017, every city, county, or city and county with a population of less than 200,000 residents, shall, in consultation with the local fire department or district and the utility director, if the city, county, or city and county operates a utility, adopt an ordinance, consistent with the goals and intent of this section, that creates an expedited, streamlined permitting process for electric vehicle charging stations. In developing an expedited permitting process, the city, county, or city and county shall adopt a checklist of all requirements with which electric vehicle charging stations shall comply to be eligible for expedited review.

An application to install an electric vehicle charging station submitted to the building official of a city, county, or city and county shall be deemed complete if, after the applicable time period described in paragraph (2) has elapsed, both of the following are true: ... An application to install an electric vehicle charging station shall be deemed approved if the applicable time period described in paragraph (2) has elapsed and all of the following are true:

Five business days after submission of the application to the city, county, or city and county, if the application is for at least 1, but not more than 25 electric vehicle charging stations at a single site. ... Twenty business days after the application was deemed complete, if the application is for at least 1, but not more than 25 electric vehicle charging stations at a single site.

citations.code_section: Cal. Gov. Code §65850.7(h)

research_notes: Access: every live sanjoseca.gov URL tried, robots.txt included, returned HTTP 403 'Access Denied' (Akamai) to curl and to WebFetch. City pages were read from raw Internet Archive captures (id_ mode, fetched with curl, tags stripped with python3, the fee schedule PDF read with pdftotext). source_url is the capture URL; the official sanjoseca.gov URL is the part after the timestamp. The captured robots.txt (https://web.archive.org/web/20260501010517/https://www.sanjoseca.gov/robots.txt) disallows only /scripts, /admin and *.asmx for all agents. The city's E-Government Policy (sanjoseca.gov/home/showdocument?id=17869, capture 20260904222013) has no rule against copying or automated access. Internet Archive terms say access 'is granted for scholarship and research purposes only'. Re-check each city quote on the live page before marking a rule verified. Quote format: list items and paragraph breaks are joined with single spaces and bullet characters are left out; ' ... ' marks omitted text; the words are verbatim. sjpermits.org robots.txt is 'User-agent: * / Disallow: /', so the SJPermits portal was not fetched; online-permit availability comes from the city's Online Building Permits page. Municode (host of the San Jose Municipal Code) was not fetched. Its archived terms (https://web.archive.org/web/20190411032708/https://www.municode.com/terms-of-use/) say: 'You may not copy, modify, reproduce, republish, distribute, display, or transmit for commercial, non-profit or public purposes all or any portion of this Website, except to the extent permitted by these Terms and Conditions of Use.' The current terms page could not be loaded. SJMC text: quotes marked 'Ord. No. 31256' come from the council-agenda redline of that ordinance (draft dated 10/16/2025, Council Agenda 10/28/2025 Item 8.2(a), file 25-1131), downloaded through the Legistar Web API (webapi.legistar.com); sanjose.granicus.com robots.txt has 'User-agent: * / Disallow: /'. Each such quote is the enacted wording: struck-through text removed and underlined additions kept, checked against the rendered PDF page. Legistar matter 25-1187 (Final Adoption of Ordinances, dated 2025-10-30) lists 'Ordinance No. 31256' as passed for publication on 10/28/2025; the signed ordinance and the final vote were not retrieved. Code edition: San Jose adopted the 2025 California codes (not 2022) for permit applications made on or after January 1, 2026. SJMC 24.09.110(A)(6) does not adopt CRC Chapter 1, Division II, so CRC §R105.2 does not apply in San Jose; the city's exemption lists are SJMC 24.02.120 to 24.02.150. Section numbering: the When Is a Building Permit Required? page (updated 06/12/2025) cites 'Section 24.02.110' for the exempt list, but Ord. No. 31256 amends the exemption lists as 24.02.120 (building), 24.02.130 (plumbing), 24.02.140 (mechanical) and 24.02.150 (electrical). Fees: the fee schedule capture is the FY 2025-26 schedule ('Effective August 11, 2025', document 26047 version 637922894017900000, captured 2025-12-07). The Building Permit Fees page captured 2026-08-01 still says the schedule shows fees in effect as of August 11, 2025, but links a newer upload (version 639180865996470000) with no capture, so the current PDF could not be compared. A draft FY 2026-27 fee resolution (Council Agenda 06-09-2026 Item 3.4(b), Legistar file 26-683) sets different amounts ('Water Heater Replacement – Permit Center 0.25 x # of units $52'); its adoption was not confirmed, so it is not cited. New param: charger_level (enum 'level_1_120v' | 'level_2_240v'), following the city's definitions: Level 1 uses a standard 120-volt outlet, Level 2 uses a 240-volt outlet. The EV page sets the permit line by level, so install_type alone cannot decide it. charger_level is not in packages/core/src/projects.ts, so validate-data will reject this file until it is added. Conflict check: SJMC 24.02.150(1) exempts connecting approved portable electrical equipment to approved permanently installed receptacles. The city's EV page says a Level 2 station 'Requires an electrical permit' without an exception for plug-in units. This record follows the EV page, which is more specific; a plug-in Level 2 unit on an existing 240-volt receptacle is therefore REQUIRED here, and that reading should be confirmed with the city. Baseline: ca-baseline/ev-charger.json defaults to REQUIRED because state law does not address plug-in chargers; San Jose's Level 1 rule governs in San Jose. docs_required lists what the EV page says to provide at a Level 2 inspection; it does not apply to a Level 1 plug-in.
